_comment: Phonetic respellings applied BEFORE TTS chunking for both eddington-1919-eclipse.json (long-form, F5-TTS-MLX sarah.wav) and eddington-1919-eclipse-short.json (Kokoro am_michael). Carries the channel-level rule from feedback_pronunciation_pretts: rewrite narration before TTS so neither model has to phonetically guess foreign / proper nouns. Mapping is applied as case-sensitive whole-word replacement by pipeline.audio.normalize_for_tts (or by a pre-render filter in render_long_form.py / render_footage_only.py).

respellings.MNRAS: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
respellings.GW150914: G W one five oh nine one four

_class_of_bug_notes: Kokoro am_michael reads 'Eddington' as ED-ding-ton (double-d articulation lands wrong); the respelling forces a clean ED-ing-tun.
F5-TTS-MLX sarah.wav reads 'Príncipe' as 'prin-SIPP-ee' (English 'principle'); respelling to PRIN-si-pay forces the Portuguese pronunciation.
Both TTS providers default to 'EEN-stine' (German/American compromise) for Einstein — the documentary register wants the standard ICE-stine. Apply globally.
Numeric arcsecond values must be word-spelled BEFORE TTS — both providers digit-spell '1.75' as 'one-point-seven-five' inconsistently (Kokoro sometimes reads it as 'one-decimal-seven-five').

Acronyms (GR, GPS, JPL, LIGO, MLX) must either be expanded in narration (GR → 'general relativity') OR letter-spelled. Kokoro reads single-syllable acronyms as words ('LIGO' → /'laɪgoʊ/ which is correct here — preserved). 'MLX' renders as 'mleeks' on Kokoro — letter-spell.
All numeric date forms in narration are already word-spelled (e.g. 'nineteen-nineteen', not '1919'). This carries forward the channel rule for any future Cosmos Decoded long-form.
